LESSON: POPULATION STRUCTURE - KENYA - GERMANY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and relationships
Topic 3.4: Population Structure - Kenya - Germany
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Population Structure - Kenya - Germany, part of People and relationships in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is population structure of a country important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify sources of population data in a country,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain factors determining population structure in Kenya and Germany,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. construct age-sex population pyramids of developed and developing countries,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. determine the significance of population structure in distribution of national resources in a society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the differences between developed and developing countries for sustainable development. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Population Structure - Kenya - Germany together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: Learners undertake the task of drawing and displaying age-sex population pyramids of

developed and developing countries (Germany and Kenya).

• Communication and collaboration: Learners work collaboratively as they discuss the significance of population structure in

distribution of national resources in a society.

Values:
● Unity: Learners collaborate with others as they brainstorm on sources of population data.

● Respect: Learners appreciate diverse opinions as they brainstorm on sources of population data.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Citizenship: Learners acquire knowledge on population structure of Kenya and Germany together with its influence on

distribution of resources in society.

● Effective Communication: Learners engage a resource person as they discuss factors determining population structure in

Kenya and Germany.

Link to other learning areas:

● Learners employ mathematics knowledge to draw and display in class population structure of Kenya and Germany.

● Learners communicate effectively as they discuss in groups the significance of population structure in distribution of national

resources in a society helping them develop language skills in English, Kiswahili, and Kenyan Sign Language.
